title.narrative: Effective, transparent and gender responsive labour market governance established

description.narrative: Bangladesh’s labour market governance faces persistent challenges in labour inspection, occupational safety and health (OSH), and industrial safety. While progress has been made, especially after events like Rana Plaza, inspection systems still fall short of ILO Convention No. 81. OSH policies remain only partially aligned, with gaps in worker protections, employer responsibilities, institutional capacity, and coordination. Industrial safety frameworks are fragmented, and risks now extend beyond the ready-made garment (RMG) sector to other high-risk areas such as food processing and chemical storage. ILO’s strategy supports stronger labour governance aligned with international standards. It assists the Government of Bangladesh in reforming labour inspection policies, adopting strategic compliance, improving digital tools like the Labour Inspection Management Application (LIMA) system and labour helpline, and mainstreaming gender across key institutions – Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE), Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments (DIFE), Department of Labour (DoL). The ILO also supports updating OSH regulations, implementing the National Plan of Action on OSH, operationalizing the National OSH Training and Research Institute (NOSHTRI), and launching youth-oriented safe work programmes. For industrial safety, ILO helps implement a coordinated framework that goes beyond RMG, supports the Industrial Safety Unit (ISU), and strengthens chemical and fire safety in depots and other hazardous settings. Expected results include stronger institutional capacity, safer workplaces, and a more unified industrial safety system. Primary beneficiaries include workers in both formal and informal sectors, employers, and labour institutions. Key partners are MoLE, DIFE, DoL, relevant ministries, employers’ and workers’ groups, industry bodies, UN agencies, and international development partners.
